questions.text: What defines a market uptrend on a stock price chart?
options: A series of higher highs and higher lows
A continuous horizontal range of prices
A series of lower highs and lower lows
A price sitting consistently below its moving average
questions.explanation: An uptrend is characterized by prices making higher highs and higher lows over a given period.

questions.text: In technical analysis, what happens when a stock price successfully breaks above a previous resistance ceiling?
options: The stock immediately enters an oversold status
The former resistance ceiling frequently transforms into a new support floor
The stock's trading volume drops to zero
The moving average automatically flips direction
questions.explanation: Once a stock breaks through a resistance level, that previous ceiling often becomes its new support level on subsequent pullbacks.

questions.text: True or false: A Relative Strength Index (RSI) reading above 70 indicates that a stock is considered oversold.
questions.explanation: An RSI reading above 70 indicates that a stock is overbought, whereas a reading below 30 indicates it is oversold.

questions.text: True or false: Position sizing determines the number of shares to buy based on the maximum amount of capital you are willing to risk on a single trade.
questions.explanation: Position sizing aligns your order size with your predetermined portfolio risk limit rather than total cash balance.
